q1.prompt: A storage browser must call sizeBytes() and render() on both files and arbitrarily nested folders. Which pattern matches that recursive shape?

choices.label: Composite: File and Folder share Entry; Folder combines child results
Give files and folders unrelated APIs and branch in every caller

wrong1.prompt: The client should not repeat the tree recursion.
wrong1.explanation: Composite puts the shared operation on leaves and containers. A folder delegates recursively, so clients can treat any Entry uniformly.

q2.prompt: A root contains a 2 MB file and a folder with 3 MB and 5 MB files. What does root.sizeBytes() return, and what is the traversal cost?

choices.label: 10 MB, with O(n) work across the entries visited
5 MB in O(1), because every component has the same interface

wrong2.prompt: Uniform syntax does not make traversal free.
wrong2.explanation: The folder sums 3 + 5 MB, then the root adds 2 MB. Composite hides the branching from the caller, not the O(n) walk through descendants.

q3.prompt: The UI calls sizeBytes() 60 times per second on a million-entry tree. What is the right response?

choices.label: Cache aggregate sizes with invalidation, or compute outside the render loop
Keep the repeated full-tree walk because sizeBytes() looks like a getter

wrong3.prompt: A simple method name can hide expensive work.
wrong3.explanation: Composite operations may traverse the whole subtree. A hot path needs cached aggregates or a different update strategy with an explicit invalidation cost.

success.prompt: You used one component contract while keeping the recursive time cost visible.
